`learn.py` applies the legacy-to-`SPECSTRIDE_*` environment name mapping at import.
The adjustable-knob allowlist is the locked literal set {`proposer_timeout`, `yield_poll_interval`}; a former third knob `inject_yield_hint` was removed.
Hard minimums: `proposer_timeout` 900 s, `yield_poll_interval` 10 s.
Hard maximums: `yield_poll_interval` 300 s fixed; `proposer_timeout` 2 x the supplied default.
Every numeric knob moves at most ±50 % per step from the value currently in effect (or the default when none is applied).
No suggestion is made (value null) with fewer than 3 samples: `work_sec_samples` for `proposer_timeout`.
No `yield_poll_interval` suggestion is made with fewer than 3 `job_duration_samples`.

The `proposer_timeout` target is 1.25 x the phase's `work_sec_p90` (p50 when p90 is missing), clamped to the step window and hard bounds, rounded to the nearest 60 s, then clamped to the hard bounds again.
The `yield_poll_interval` target is 0.1 x the phase's `job_duration_p50`, clamped to the step window and [10, 300], rounded to a whole second.
When the step window and the hard bounds do not overlap, the hard bounds alone are used.
`resolve` clamps a stored value into [hard min, hard max] at read time and always prints an integer.
A decision applies only to the phase shape it was learned under: a decision recorded under another shape, or under no shape, resolves to the default.
The effective value is a last-one-wins replay of the decision entries (`apply` and `revert`; `evaluate` entries never move a value; entries without `action` count as decisions).

`<feature-dir>/learning/applied.json` is a JSON-lines decision log opened in append mode (one entry per apply/revert/evaluate); the directory is created on demand and existing lines are never rewritten.
Learning events are appended to `<feature-dir>/events.jsonl` (the feature directory itself, not a run's `runs/<id>/events.jsonl`) unless `--events-file` is given.
An `apply` entry has the fields `schema`, `action=apply`, `run_id`, `knob`, `phase`, `shape`, `value`, `previous`, `samples`, `source_runs`, `metric`, `applied_at`, `baseline`.
The applied-entry schema written is `specstride.learn.applied/2`; `/1` entries are still read but never match a shape.

An apply entry's `baseline` holds `backend`, `shape`, `runs`, `cost` and `wall` sample lists of `[run, value]`, and `guardrails` counts; runs under another backend label or flagged tampered are left out.
A `revert` entry has `schema`, `action=revert`, a new `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`, `knob`, `phase`, `shape`, `value` (the apply's `previous`), `previous` (the apply's `value`), `applied_at`.
An automatic revert entry additionally carries `auto: true`, `guardrail` (list), `evaluated_from`, `quarantined_value`, `backend`, `reverted_ts`.
An `evaluate` entry is the evaluation result plus `schema`, `action=evaluate`, a new `run_id` and `evaluated_at`; it never modifies the apply entry.
Generated decision run ids are `learn-` followed by 12 hex characters.

The observation document (`observe --out`, conventionally `<feature-dir>/learning/phase-<N>.json`) has `schema`, `phase`, `shape`, `generated_at`, `observation`, `inputs` and is overwritten whole on each call.
The summary document has `schema` = `specstride.learn.summary/7`, `inputs`, `runs`, `attempts`, `phases`, `totals`.
Events files are read leniently: blank lines, non-JSON lines (a half-written tail) and JSON values without an `event` key are skipped.
Verdict transcripts are read for the byte size of the section between the `═══════════ PROMPT ═══════════` and `═══════════ REPLY ═══════════` markers.
A transcript is matched to the (phase, attempt) whose verdict time is nearest to the transcript's local timestamp, within 900 s.
Gate-duration files are JSON with a `commands` list; `durationMs` is summed and the `live` share is the part from commands whose `args` or `executable` contain `live`.
`knob_adjusted` (apply of `proposer_timeout`): fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `from`, `to`, `reason`, `metric`, `samples`, `run_id`; no `time` field is written.
`knob_adjusted` (apply of `yield_poll_interval`): same fields, `metric=job_duration_p50`.
`knob_adjusted` (revert): fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `from`, `to`, `reason`, `samples=null`, `metric=null`, `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`.
`knob_auto_reverted`: fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `guardrail` (comma-joined names), `from`, `to`, `run_id`, `reverts_run_id`; emitted after the `knob_adjusted` of the same revert.
`knob_evaluated`: fields `event`, `ts`, `knob`, `phase`, `label`, `action`, `reset`, `cost_r`, `cost_mde`, `wall_r`, `wall_mde`, `n_applied`, `n_baseline`, `run_id`, `evaluates_run_id`.
`knob_adjusted reason=learned_from_work_sec_p90` (apply of `proposer_timeout`).
`knob_adjusted reason=learned_from_job_duration_p50` (apply of `yield_poll_interval`).
`knob_adjusted reason=revert` (manual `revert` and `off`).
`knob_adjusted reason=auto_revert` (guardrail breach during evaluate).
`knob_evaluated action` is `evaluated`, `auto_reverted` or `skipped_superseded`.
The `ts` of learning events is the string form of `time.time()` (epoch seconds).
Events without a `run_id` are attributed to the run id last seen in the same file; events seen before any run id in that file are dropped.
`run_start` is read for `ts`, `feature`, `backend`, `resume`.
`phase_start` is read for `phase`, `title`, `shape`; it resets the current attempt and pass.
`proposer_start` is read for `phase`, `attempt` and sets the attempt start time.
`iter_start` is read for `iter`; it opens a pass in the current attempt.
`agent_tool` is read for `tool` and `target`; each counts one tool call, and a `Bash` target is classified wait vs work.
`agent_result` is read for `is_error`, `duration_ms`, `cost_usd`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `output_tokens`.
`yield_resume` is read for `job_duration_sec`, else `waited_sec`.
`pass_killed` is read for `reason` (default `unknown`), `elapsed`, `detail`.
`iter_done` is read for `evidence`; any value other than absent or `missing` marks the pass as having written evidence.
`evidence_written` increments the attempt's evidence count and marks the current pass productive.
`verification_passed` / `verification_failed` are read for `phase`, `attempt`, `rc` (failed only).
`critic_start` is read for its `ts`; `critic_sec` is the time to the following `verdict`.
`diagnostician_done` is read for `case` (default `unknown`).
`grounding_gap` is read for `paths` (comma-separated).
`verdict` is read for `phase`, `attempt`, `result`, `reason`.
`phase_done` and `attempt_archived` close an attempt that has no end time yet.
`proposer_cap` is read for `phase`, `seconds`, `source`, `yield_poll`, `yield_poll_source`, `arm`, `yield_poll_arm`, `tamper_bracket`; only the first per (run, phase) counts.
`events_tampered` marks the whole run as tampered; the run is excluded from every baseline and evaluation.
`run_stop` is read for `reason` and `phase`.

A Bash target is a wait call when it matches `sleep <n>`, `tail -f|-c`, `while pgrep|true`, `until grep`, `pgrep -`, `ps aux ... grep` or `watch -n`, or declares any `sleep` seconds; declared sleep seconds are summed.
Kill classes: `hard_cap` = budget, `repeat_stall` and `progress_stall` = futility, `idle_timeout` = hang; other reasons = unknown.
Pass outcome: `budget_kill` (killed for `hard_cap`), `worker_error` (any other kill, or `is_error`), `open` (no result yet), `productive` (evidence written), else `clean_no_progress`.
A pass is billed when it is closed and its result carried `cost_usd`; while open `billed` is null.
`work_sec_estimate` = max(0, sum of pass elapsed − declared sleep seconds); attempts with any futility kill are excluded from the phase's `work_sec` samples.
Percentiles use linear interpolation between sorted samples and are rounded to 0.1.
With phase shapes given, a phase's figures use only attempts recorded under that shape; a phase with none is omitted from `phases`, and `other_shape_attempts` counts those left out.
The evaluation sample unit is a billed pass that was not killed for futility.
A primary (cost or wall) is `insufficient` unless both arms have at least 6 samples.
The effect r is the difference of mean log values (applied − baseline); `helped` when r <= −MDE, `regressed` when r >= MDE, else `neutral`.
MDE = 2.80 x max(sd, 0.50) x sqrt(1/n_a + 1/n_b) x sqrt(1 + (mean passes per episode − 1) x 0.5).
Values are floored before the log: cost at 0.0001, wall at 1.0 s.
The combined label is `regressed` if either primary regressed, else `helped` if either helped, else `neutral` if either is neutral, else `insufficient`.
Evaluation reason `no baseline recorded (applied before evaluate existed)` gives label `insufficient`.
Evaluation `reset=shape`: the phase's shape changed since the decision; label `insufficient`.
Evaluation `reset=backend`: the phase's latest run used another backend label than the baseline; label `insufficient` and applied-arm samples are discarded.

A run belongs to a decision's applied arm when its `proposer_cap` recorded arm `applied` with the decision's value and `tamper_bracket=on`; with no arm recorded, when the source is `learned` at that value. The decision's own source runs are never in its applied arm.
The counterfactual for `proposer_timeout` is `censored` for a longer cap, `shorter_cap_wall_only` for a shorter one, `none` otherwise; it never feeds the label.
The arbitration proxy counts episodes whose run stopped at the phase with reason `max_rejects`, `gate_oscillation`, `critic_config` or `proposer_no_progress`.

Guardrail states are `ok`, `breach` or `unknown`; a rate guardrail is `unknown` below 10 applied-arm trials, and breaches when the exact one-sided binomial tail against the baseline rate is below 0.01.
The baseline rate is shrunk to (k + 0.5) / (n + 1).
Guardrail names: `grounding_gap_rate`, `malformed_rate`, `verification`, `diagnostician_grounding_share`, `critic_input_size`, `arbitration_proxy`, `first_attempt_approval` (two-sided).
The `verification` guardrail breaches at any n when the applied arm has a failed verification and the baseline had none; with no applied attempts it is `unknown`.
The `critic_input_size` guardrail needs 6 prompt sizes per arm and breaches on an exact rank test with p < 0.01.
A guardrail breach makes a non-dry-run `evaluate` revert the decision automatically (the only automatic write to a decision), recording the evaluation with `action_taken=auto_reverted`.
If a newer apply overtook the evaluated decision, the breach is recorded as `action_taken=skipped_superseded` and nothing is reverted; after a manual revert or `off` it is a silent no-op.
An evaluation is recorded (entry + `knob_evaluated`) only when its signature (label, reset, action, arm sizes, guardrail states) differs from the last evaluation of the same decision.

Quarantine: after an automatic revert, a suggested value within ±10 % of the reverted value for the same (knob, phase, shape, backend) is refused until 6 new non-futility samples from runs started after the revert exist.
`evaluate` without `--specs`/`--phase-shape` treats each decision's own recorded shape as the current shape, so no shape reset is reported.
